why: Owner report 2026-11-06: the article writer is producing hard-to-read pieces. Four classes hold a publish because they are deterministic (an executive summary at the foot of the page, a bullet carrying two statistics, two citations in one sentence, a run-on source list). The prose classes (read-twice, timeline repetition, cold closing concept) are reported to the rewrite and the reviewer and never hold: they are heuristics over grammar, and a heuristic that cannot see paraphrase must not reject an article. Owner directive 2026-11-07 added the diction and structure classes he named on a live dispatch: private shorthand nouns ('the fact', 'hop owner', 'the wire'), a heading that promises a count without labelling its items, a multi-variable comparison left in prose with no table, and a Sources block whose entries carry no list marker (so the CMS renders one paragraph).

banned_nouns.label: the fact
banned_nouns.remedy: name the state — session state, execution state or context payload

banned_nouns.label: hop owner
banned_nouns.remedy: name the role — systems architect, service owner or calling agent

banned_nouns.label: the wire
banned_nouns.remedy: name the layer — the protocol layer, the connection or the request

banned_nouns.label: the line
banned_nouns.remedy: name the revision that moved — the July 2026 MCP revision
